newsitem.title: UK: Proton plans immediate Lotus boost.
newsitem.headline: Proton plans immediate Lotus boost.

text.p: The chairman of Malaysian carmaker Proton said on Wednesday the company planned an immediate increase in production of the Elise sportscar manufacured by its newly acquired Lotus associate.
"With our contribution we can expand Lotus production here...we will expand capacity immediately," said Yahaya Ahmad.

He said the company hoped to bring production up to 10 cars per day from the current five and additional capacity to serve Far Eastern markets would be added at Proton plants in Malaysia to give total Elise production capacity of about 5,000 cars per year.
"Initially, I think we should be able to build 2,500 annually in Malaysia - it's not going to be big numbers," Ahmad added.
Proton made 160,000 cars in 1995 and has ambitious plans to produce 500,000 year by the end of this decade.
Earlier, the company said it would invest 51 million stg for an 80 pct stake in Lotus and provide a loan of 13 million stg to cover working capital. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
